name: bzip2
description: Compresses single files with a stronger (but slower) algorithm than gzip; pairs with tar via -j.

examples.explanation: tar with bzip2 filter (-j) — better ratio than -z at the cost of speed.

about: bzip2 typically achieves 10–15% better compression than gzip but is several times slower, which is why xz (better ratio, comparable speed to bzip2) and zstd (nearly gzip speed, near-xz ratio) have largely displaced it. Support is universal, so old .bz2 archives remain fully accessible.
mistakes: Choosing bzip2 for new workflows where xz or zstd would serve better.
